items.item_text: 01. All applicants are required to submit responses to the following supplemental questions. Your responses will provide information about your background and experience related to this position and will be used in the screening and selection process. Be concise yet specific and informative in your responses to these supplemental questions. "See resume," attachments or links will not be accepted as a substitute for your responses to the questions in the following boxes. Incomplete responses will not be considered. Please indicate below that you have read and understand these instructions. Options: Yes | No

02. I understand that my application will be considered incomplete if any required sections of the application are not completed and/or if any documents that are required are not attached to my online application by the closing date. Options: Yes | No

03. Do you possess a valid Class "C" California driver's license and have the ability to maintain insurability under the District’s vehicle insurance policy? Options: Yes | No | No, but I am able to obtain one
04. Please specify your highest level of education: Options: High School or equivalent (GED) | Associate's Degree | Bachelor's Degree | Master's Degree | Juris Doctor | Doctorate Degree
05. Do you possess a Bachelor's Degree in from an accredited institution in criminal justice, administration of justice, public administration, or a related field. Options: Yes | No
06. Do you possess a Masters Degree in from an accredited institution in criminal justice, administration of justice, public administration, or a related field. Options: Yes | No
07. If applicable, please list indicate the degrees and field in which you have earned your degree/s in (type N/A if not applicable):
08. Do you possess a POST Management Certificate? Options: Yes | No and not willing to obtain | No, but willing to obtain within 12 months of appointment
09. Do you possess a POST Executive Certificate? Options: Yes | No | No, but it is in progress

10. Indicate the full-time equivalent years of progressively responsible law enforcement experience Options: Zero to 1 year | 2 to 3 years | 4 to 5 years | 6 to 7 years | 8 years | 9 years | 10 years | 11 years | 12 years | 13 years or more

11. Indicate where you have worked to obtain progressive experience in law enforcement. What was the time frame? What was the employer's name? Describe the work you performed. [This section is required.]
12. How many years of experience do you have in a Sergeant rank or higher? Options: None | 1 year | 2 years | 3 years | 4 years | 5 years | 6 years | 7 years | 8 years | 9 or more years

13. If applicable, please indicate where you have worked to obtain experience in a Sergeant rank or higher (type N/A, if not applicable). What was the time frame? What was the employer's name? Describe the work performed. This section is required.
14. Do you have command experience with a college or university police department? Options: Yes | No

15. Please note Pasadena City College police officers do not carry firearms. Please acknowledge your understanding of this. Selecting Decline will disqualify you for this position. Options: I Acknowledge | I Decline

16. Describe how you have demonstrated sensitivity and understanding in delivery of services and support to a diverse workforce and student population (diverse in terms of socioeconomic, cultural, disability, gender identity, sexual orientation, and ethnic background). This section is required.
Possession of a POST Management Certificate at the time of appointment, or obtain within twelve (12) months of appointment
Possession of, or progress toward, the POST Executive Certificate
Possession of a valid California driver's license and the ability to maintain insurability under the District's vehicle insurance policy.
Bachelor's degree from an accredited institution in criminal justice, administration of justice, public administration, or a related field.
Master's degree in a related field
Eight (8) years of progressively responsible law enforcement experience.
Command experience with a college or university police department
Five (5) years of experience at the rank of Sergeant or higher

Directs the planning, organizing, and evaluating of all operations related to Campus Police & Safety Services and implementation of new or revised services to ensure maintenance of a safe campus, protection of life and property, regulation of traffic, citation, apprehension, and arrest of law violators, campus-to-community involvement, and maintenance of police records. Manages full- and part-time staff, including sworn police officers and investigators, and cadet corps. Oversees operations of parking, dispatch, safety, and emergency planning and operations.

Takes immediate command of all law enforcement activities during major emergencies, tactical events, and unusual or complex incidents, serving as Incident Commander during police operations; directs the District's emergency operations, disaster response, and business continuity planning and serves on management and response teams overseeing the District's involvement in tactical events.

Directs the activities of senior-level law enforcement and civilian personnel to ensure departmental functions are meeting the overall needs and goals of the department and the District. Develops and directs implementation of policy and procedural changes resulting from changes in legislation, procedures, or District policy.

Serves as and exercises the powers of a sworn peace officer pursuant to the provisions of California State Penal Code Section 830.32 and Education Code Section 72330, while engaged in the performance of the duties within this employment.

Ensures all sworn personnel meet POST training and certification requirements and that all other personnel are properly trained, including de-escalation, crisis intervention, diversity, and cultural competency training for officers and cadets; mentors subordinates on leadership and the resolution of personnel, procedural, and operational problems.

Ensures the integrity, security, and chain of custody of police records and evidence; compiles data and prepares reports for District leadership and for county, state, and federal agencies, including the annual crime statistics and security disclosures required under the Clery Act.

Administers various functions beyond law enforcement, including coordinating assistance during medical emergencies; preventing fires, fire hazards, theft, and vandalism; monitoring and maintaining campus burglar, fire, and other building alarm systems; and investigating and reporting unusual, hazardous, or suspicious occurrences and conditions.
